reviews.review: Decent game. If you're a 40K fanatic you will LOVE this.

tldr; Play this game, it's good, buy it if it's okay with your budget. You don't need to know or like anything about WH40K to enjoy it. Play this good game so they can make a great sequel. The game hits so many good spots, it'd be really dissappointing to see it being forgotten.

edit: play time doesn't reflect my gameplay time, as I played it completely offline for the most part.

Entertaining, good controls, sound design is stunning, the graphics are very well for its age and overall, the gameplay is solid. The game puts a lot of cool stuff on the table but gives you massive blue balls, as almost all of its features could have been so much better. For example, finishers on stunned enemies are a lot of fun but some of the animations take too long and the variety is limited. Another example, your weapons feel really great to use (especially thanks to the sounds) but they could have felt much better if dismemberment and gore were implemented. I don't like the fact that I'm shooting a full auto rocket launcher but it has the same effect on the enemy as a 5.56 rifle. Enemy variety is fine, could be better (with more races from WH40k). Only a few times, the game made me say "that's bullcrap", the difficulty is well balanced. With all its great sound design, I wish music design was also better. Now that I think about it, this game could use all the lessons we learned from DOOM(2016) but obviously, SEGA would need a time machine. Please please PLEASE someone make a decent sequel for this game! 

Oh and there is multiplayer but its pretty much just a gimmick. I wish the coop horde shooter nature of the multiplayer was emphasized, for example, I'd love to play the campaign with my friends, rather than useless AI. Chaos Marines look cool though, and overall, the customization is fairly decent.

Played this on Xbox 360 then bought it again on PC when my Xbox went belly up.

It's a hugely satisfying experience for any Warhammer 40k fan. It has flaws, for sure. And I remember the melee fighting feeling very chaotic and difficult at times and not in a good way. But when you chainsword a few dozen orks in half it does feel pretty good.

Above all I just remember the feeling of actually getting to be immersed into 40k. It's certainly a very one-sided sort of experience, you are the noble space marine and everyone else is a bad guy meat bag waiting to turned into sushi, but you really feel like a geneticly forged super soldier clad in the finest armor and by the end you will have honed your skills as finely as any chapter veteran.

It's a good game. Certainly not the best game ever, but if you like 40k then you need to experience this.

This is another classic example of a game whose presentation is so well executed that it is good in spite of its own shortcomings. From the stompy sound our human wrecking ball protagonist makes, to the visceral squishing sound an ork makes after being split apart, the sound direction is sublime. The 40K visual aesthetic is followed loyally and readably, in a way that somehow immerses despite its comedic grim-darkness.  And the multiplayer ain't bad to boot! Maybe one day we'll see a Space Marine 2. It can be an apology for Dawn of War 3.

This game goes to be at a place where some other stood and fell. Warhammer 40k games are really common these days and while some of them are not bad and definetly playable only some of them seem to be called "good". 

This one is very much the latter. It has a nice campaign mode with atleast some hours of fun in it, a multiplayer mode and a coop survival mode. The last one got my attention very much where I fight with my friends through all the hordes of orcs.

Too bad no one plays the multiplayer any more.
